content: Oxacillin is an antibiotic used to treat infections caused by specific types of bacteria. It works by inhibiting the bacteria's ability to form their cell walls, which ultimately kills the bacteria. However, it is not effective against viral infections such as the common cold, influenza, or coronavirus, nor does it work for non-bacterial infections. Using oxacillin or any antibiotic unnecessarily can lead to antibiotic resistance, making future bacterial infections harder to treat. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding It is not known whether oxacillin can harm an unborn baby or affect pregnancy. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your healthcare provider. They will determine whether oxacillin is appropriate for you during pregnancy. Oxacillin does pass into breast milk, so if you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed, discuss this with your healthcare provider to assess potential risks. Drug Interactions There are no known interactions between oxacillin and food or drinks. However, the effects of alcohol on oxacillin are unclear. Heavy alcohol consumption can weaken your immune system, making it harder for your body to fight infections. Always inform your healthcare provider about all medications, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are taking. Specific drugs, such as tetracyclines (e.g., doxycycline, minocycline) or probenecid (commonly used for gout), may interact with oxacillin. This list may not be exhaustive, so consult your healthcare provider for more details. Dosage and Administration Oxacillin is typically administered as an injection into a muscle or vein by a healthcare provider in a hospital or clinic setting. It is available in various forms, including 1 g, 2 g, 10 g injections, and 20 mg/mL or 40 mg/mL solutions. If you are storing oxacillin at home, keep it out of reach of children and do not share it with others, even if they have similar symptoms. Missed Dose and Overdose If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double the dose. Completing the full prescribed course of oxacillin is crucial, even if your symptoms improve, to prevent antibiotic resistance. In case of an overdose, seek immediate medical attention by calling 911 or contacting a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Common Side Effects The most common side effects of oxacillin include pain, swelling, or inflammation at the injection site and rash. If these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. There may be other side effects not listed here, so contact your provider if you suspect any adverse reactions. Serious Side Effects 1. Severe Allergic Reactions: Symptoms include difficulty breathing, wheezing, rapid heartbeat, fever, swollen lymph nodes, facial swelling, throat tightness, hives, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, or fainting. Stop using oxacillin and seek immediate medical attention if these occur. 2. Seizures: Some individuals have reported seizures while using oxacillin. Signs include muscle twitching, jerking, spasms, tremors, stiffening of limbs, confusion, anxiety, dizziness, or loss of consciousness. Discontinue use and contact your healthcare provider if you experience these symptoms. 3. Kidney Damage: Symptoms include reduced urination, swelling in the feet or legs, unusual fatigue, chest pain, shortness of breath, confusion, or nausea. Notify your healthcare provider immediately if these occur. 4. Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea: Overgrowth of Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) in the gut can cause severe diarrhea, even up to two months after stopping the antibiotic. Symptoms include watery diarrhea, persistent diarrhea, blood in stool, severe stomach cramps, or fever. Contact your healthcare provider if these symptoms develop. 5. Blood Disorders: Oxacillin can cause conditions such as eosinophilia, agranulocytosis, neutropenia, or bone marrow suppression. Symptoms include fever, pale or yellowish skin, easy bruising or bleeding, frequent infections, unusual fatigue, dizziness, or abnormal heartbeat. Stop using oxacillin and seek medical help if these occur. 6. Liver Damage: Symptoms of liver damage include nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, fever, fatigue, itching, loss of appetite, light-colored stool, dark urine, or yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice). Contact your healthcare provider immediately if these symptoms arise. Precautions Do not use oxacillin if you are allergic to it or any of its ingredients. Inform your pharmacist or healthcare provider about any allergies, including to penicillin, other medications, or corn products. Additionally, disclose any history of asthma, liver or kidney problems, or antibiotic-associated diarrhea. This information will help your provider determine if oxacillin is safe and appropriate for you. Summary Oxacillin is a powerful antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections but must be used responsibly to avoid resistance and adverse effects. Always follow your healthcare provider's instructions and report any concerning symptoms promptly.
